maximum_permitted_stay: Up to 3 months; initial period may be extended by 60 days in two intervals.
passport_validity_rule: At least 6 months from intended arrival.
blank_passport_pages_rule: No minimum blank-page count stated in the current NCIC tourist checklist.
return_ticket_rule: Travel itinerary or booking required; a separate return-ticket document is not specified.
proof_of_funds_rule: No fixed proof-of-funds item in the tourist checklist; additional documents may be requested.
accommodation_rule: Hotel booking or reservation; if using other accommodation, provide the address.
travel_insurance_rule: Not specified in the reviewed official tourist-visa guidance.
yellow_fever_or_health_rule: No yellow-fever vaccination certificate is mandatory for entry under the NCIC notice dated 2 October 2026. The separate transit-visa page still lists a yellow-fever certificate, so transit applicants should confirm whether that checklist has been updated.
transit_rule: Separate online transit visa for travel through Uganda to a third country; maximum 7 days, non-extendable, USD50. The transit page still lists a yellow-fever certificate, but the 2 October 2026 NCIC notice says it is not mandatory for entry; confirm transit-specific instructions. No Bangladesh-specific airside exemption verified.
application_channel: Official online portal; approval letter required before travel; no visa on arrival; biometric capture at immigration office/border after approval.
application_fee: USD 50; non-refundable; payment subject to a bank charge.
processing_time: Less than 3 working days (NCIC 12 Oct 2023); apply at least 10 days ahead per NCIC notice; estimate, not guarantee.
required_documents: Passport biodata page copy with at least 6 months validity|Tour plan|Travel itinerary or booking|Recent passport-size photograph|Hotel booking or reservation or other accommodation address|Documents in English|Additional documents if requested
review_notes: Bangladesh is absent from the current NCIC visa-exempt nationality list. Visa-prone travellers must apply online and obtain approval before travel; NCIC states that no visa is issued on arrival. The single-entry tourist visa may be granted for up to three months; its approval authorisation expires 90 days after approval. The official USD50 fee is non-refundable and payments are subject to a bank charge. NCIC's 12 October 2023 notice says visas take less than three working days; its earlier notice advises applying at least ten days before travel. These are estimates/advice, not guarantees. The tourist checklist requires passport bio-data copy with six months validity, tour plan, itinerary or booking, recent passport-size photograph and accommodation booking/address. The 2 October 2026 notice removes the yellow-fever certificate as an entry requirement, but the transit visa page still lists it; the scope of that transit checklist conflict should be confirmed with NCIC. Biometric capture at an immigration office or border after approval is separate from the uploaded photograph.

maximum_permitted_stay: Initial period set at entry; visitor may not remain beyond 6 months without permission.
passport_validity_rule: No numeric minimum stated on the official holiday-visa checklist; confirm any portal-specific rule.
blank_passport_pages_rule: No numeric blank-page count stated in the official holiday-visa checklist.
return_ticket_rule: If requested, evidence of readmission to domicile or last permanent residence; no fixed ticket format stated.
proof_of_funds_rule: If requested, sufficient means for maintenance and return transport during the stated visit.
accommodation_rule: Destination address required; if staying with a resident, host invitation and host proof of residence or ID.
travel_insurance_rule: Not specified in the reviewed official holiday-visa guidance.
yellow_fever_or_health_rule: No health certificate is listed in the published holiday-visa checklist; no Bangladesh-specific health rule was confirmed in the reviewed sources.
transit_rule: No Bangladesh-specific airside transit exemption verified; if entering Zimbabwe, Category C visa must be obtained before travel.
application_channel: Apply online through eVisa.gov.zw; Bangladesh Category C applicants must pay for and obtain the visa before travel.
application_fee: USD 30 ordinary single-entry online visa; Immigration may change the visa type and fee.
processing_time: Average 7 working days; may vary; not guaranteed.
required_documents: Passport photo|Passport bio-data page scan|Proof of residence|Destination address|Host invitation letter if staying with a resident|Host proof of residence or ID if hosted|Evidence of sufficient means and readmission if requested by an Immigration Officer
official_immigration_source_name: Zimbabwe Department of Immigration — Category C Countries
cross_check_source_name: Zimbabwe Department of Immigration — eVisa FAQs
review_notes: The official Category C page explicitly lists Bangladesh and requires the visa to be applied for, paid and obtained before travel. The eVisa FAQ states that a single-entry eVisa is valid for three months from issue; this is the entry-validity window, not the permitted stay. The initial stay is set at entry, and Immigration Regulations regulation 9(5) state that a visitor may not remain beyond six months without Chief Immigration Officer permission. The ordinary single-entry online visa fee is USD30; the Department reserves the right to change visa type and fee during processing. The eVisa FAQ gives an average processing estimate of seven working days and says it may vary; no three-week advance requirement was found on the reviewed official pages. The holiday checklist requires passport photo, bio-data scan, proof of residence and destination address; host invitation and host proof of residence or ID are conditional on staying with a resident. The Regulations permit an officer to request evidence of sufficient means and readmission. The reviewed official checklist states no numeric passport-validity or photo-size rule.
